verses.1: And David urged the chiefs of the tribes and the people to do all this.
verses.2: And David said to all the people of Israel, “Is it good for you? If so, then from our God, who has sent this message, let it be granted to our brothers who remain in all the lands of Israel. Let the priests and Levites also go with them to their towns in Migrashah. They will come to us.”
verses.3: And let our God’s throne be moved towards us. For it was not taken from us during the days of Shaul.
verses.4: And all the people said, “Let us do as it is right in the eyes of all the people.”
verses.5: David gathered all of Israel, from the borders of Egypt, until they arrived at the place where the Ark of God was to be brought out of the cave.
verses.6: David and all of Israel went up to the mountains that belonged to Judah, in order to take up their tents there. This was where Jehovah, the Lord who dwells in the clefts of the rock, was also worshipped.
verses.7: And they made the Ark of God onto a new cart, from the house of Abinadab, Uzzah, and his brothers. They used this cart to carry the Ark.
verses.8: And David and all of Israel sang before the Lord with all their strength, in songs, hymns, dances, and instrumental music.
verses.9: And they came to Goren Kidan. Uzza took his hand to hold the aron, because they had left it there earlier in the day.
verses.10: And Jehovah struck Uziah, and he died there, before God.
verses.11: And it happened to David that Jehovah burst forth with a great anger. He called that place “Ezer.” It’s still called Ezer to this day.
verses.12: David feared the Lord on that day, and he said, “How shall I bring the Ark of God to me?”
verses.13: And David did not take the ark to his city. Instead, he carried it to the house of Adam Haggith.
verses.14: And the Lord dwelt with the servant of Adam in his house, which was a three-story building. And Jehovah blessed the servant of Adam and all who belonged to him.
